rationale: ROUND 2 — REVISE from round 1 (gating objection from editquality), and all three HIGH-severity objections were RIGHT. bugs_open/315 PLAN D7: arm the three update_page_status steps that stamp a page 'deployed' without recording what was sent, so pages.content_hash cannot go stale behind a deploy. Migration 526 (which enables the divergence check, DGH-015) gates on the recursive unarmed count being zero and currently refuses; this is what makes it appliable. WHAT ROUND 1 GOT WRONG, and what changed: (1) editquality [HIGH] warned that a loop's sub_workflow may execute via `substeps`, not `steps`, and that jsonb_set would then silently CREATE a dead key while the real step stayed unarmed — this bug's own census-blindness reproduced one level deeper, inside the migration written to fix it. CHECKED: loop_actions.go:91-104 reads config['substeps'] FIRST and falls back to sub_workflow.steps only when substeps is absent or empty, so the hazard is exactly as described. MEASURED: none of the three carries substeps (each uses sub_workflow.steps exclusively, 9/10/8 steps), so the path is right — but the migration no longer DEPENDS on that silently: a new gate refuses if any target loop carries a non-empty substeps, and it is PROVEN TO BITE by inducing that exact fault in a rolled-back transaction. (2) editquality + debug_historian [HIGH] warned that four agent types carry TWO active definition rows where only the higher version loads, so an UPDATE by type could arm a dormant row while the live one stays unarmed AND the verify would pass against the wrong row. MEASURED: our three carry one row each, and 4 other types fleet-wide do carry two, so the trap is real and simply does not bite here. Now asserted by a gate, also PROVEN TO BITE by inserting a genuine second active row in a rolled-back transaction (with a NOTICE confirming the fault actually took, because the first attempt at that test failed on a NOT NULL constraint before reaching the gate and therefore proved nothing). (3) guardian + prior_art_librarian [HIGH] refuted the central safety claim. Round 1 said 'runs in ALL HISTORY: 0, 0, 0' and argued the change was behaviourally inert. That figure came from orchestration_states, which retains terminal rows for roughly two days — MEASURED: only 24 of its 3,154 rows are older than 48h. So it meant '0 SURVIVING rows', not '0 runs'. The durable source is agent_run_stats: page-rebuild 7 runs (last 2026-08-08), pageflow-builder 3 (2026-08-09), site-work-orchestrator 1 (2026-08-09), with maintenance-triage 4 (2026-08-08) matching page-rebuild's last run to the minute. They are RARE, NOT DEAD. Control first, because a silent table proves nothing: agent_run_stats tracks 134 agent types and 85,389 runs since 2026-07-26 (so this is 'since 26 July', not 'for ever' — stated rather than repeating the same over-claim one table along). THE HAZARD IS NOT ALREADY LOOSE, and that is now structural rather than lucky: the three last ran 2026-08-09 13:50 and the first content_hash was written 2026-08-20 17:36, eleven days later, so they cannot have stranded a fingerprint — the column had no values when they last ran. That is why the fleet sweep found 228 of 228 matching. Arming is protective for their NEXT run.

plan.summary: Arm the three remaining update_page_status steps that stamp 'deployed' without recording what was sent, by naming their sibling git_commit step's output_field (page_deployed) as deploy_result_field — mirroring migration 494. Round 2 adds two gates demanded by round 1's HIGH objections (no non-empty config.substeps on the target loops; exactly one active definition row per target type), both proven to bite by induced fault, and replaces the blast-radius measurement with a retention-immune source.

edits.rationale: NEW FILE, revised after round 1's REVISE. The config migration that closes the stale-fingerprint hazard and unblocks 526. Not a _HOLD file: deploy_result_field is already declared by the running binary (494 armed three other agents on 2026-08-20; 247 fingerprints written since), and the chassis carrying the divergence check is now LIVE (v1.0.1322 / commit bac18992, ancestry verified at the artefact with a reverse-direction control, binary probed for the registered check name with a near-identical absent literal as the negative control).
edits.sketch: Three snapshot_agent() calls, then FOUR gates, then two UPDATEs, then a verify — all in one transaction. GATE 1 already-applied: recursive count of the three stamps already naming deploy_result_field = 3 -> RAISE '...already...'. GATE 2 needle: exactly 3 agents must still have a loop sub_workflow pairing a git_commit step deploy_page (output_field 'page_deployed') with a deployed-stamping update_page_status. GATE 3 single-row [NEW, round 2]: exactly 3 active definition rows across the 3 target types, because four types on this estate carry two active rows where only the higher version loads — an UPDATE by type could arm the dormant one and the verify would pass against the wrong row. PROVEN TO BITE: inserting a genuine second active page-rebuild row inside a rolled-back transaction raises '...found 4...', with a NOTICE first confirming the fault actually took. GATE 4 substeps [NEW, round 2, the gating objection]: refuse if any target loop carries a non-empty config.substeps, because LoopAction reads substeps FIRST (loop_actions.go:91-104) and jsonb_set into sub_workflow.steps would then create a DEAD key while the executing step stayed unarmed — and the recursive verify would find the armed dead copy and pass. PROVEN TO BITE by adding a substeps object to page-rebuild in a rolled-back transaction. UPDATES: jsonb_set into {workflow,steps,build_pages_loop,config,sub_workflow,steps,update_page_status,config,deploy_result_field} for page-rebuild + pageflow-builder, and {...,build_items_loop,...} for site-work-orchestrator — written explicitly rather than via one shared expression, because the loop step is named differently on the third. On debug_historian's concurrent-edit point: each UPDATE takes a row lock and jsonb_set operates on the row's CURRENT value, not the value the gates read, so a concurrent session's other keys survive and only a concurrent write to this one key could be lost; gates, UPDATEs and verify are one transaction. snapshot_agent() backs up but does not lock, and the file says so. VERIFY AS A RAISE, not SELECTs (ON_ERROR_STOP does not fire on a non-empty result): assert all 3 armed with page_deployed, AND assert the FLEET-WIDE unarmed count is now 0 — the second is what 526 gates on and it catches a fourth stamper appearing meanwhile.

bugs_open/336: this lane armed stampers on 2026-08-20 and took every page-publish in the estate down for 33 minutes by verifying config and never asking whether a page could still publish — hence damage-query-first in this file's header
plan.risks: Round 1's 'behaviourally inert' claim is WITHDRAWN as unsound: these three are rare, not dead — 11 runs between them in ~26 days, last activity 2026-08-09. The single behaviour change when they run is the intended one: refuse the 'deployed' stamp when the deploy step reported a skip, which is the defect bugs_open/315 exists to fix. Failure mode if evidence cannot be resolved is FAIL-OPEN by design (stamp anyway, log DEPLOY_EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE at warning), so a mistake produces noise, not a stall. The 33-minute outage this lane caused on 2026-08-20 was a StrictConfig rejection of an UNDECLARED key; that key is now declared and proven live by three armed agents and 247 fingerprints, so that specific failure cannot recur. WHAT I AM STILL LESS SURE OF, stated: (1) agent_run_stats itself only begins 2026-07-26, so 'lifetime' means 'since 26 July' — a run before that is invisible to me, though it would only strengthen the case for arming; (2) I have not OBSERVED any of these three run, so the armed path is unexercised on them — the header therefore directs the applier to the damage query first rather than to the benefit; (3) guardian's round-1 point that this lane touching this mechanism class again warrants a second pair of eyes beyond the council stands, and is not something a resubmission can discharge — it is a judgement for the owner, and the migration is deliberately NOT applied pending it.
